category_title: Students who openly challenge teacher misidentification or disrespect
minimal_context: The student is participating in a sound association word identification game projected on a screen in the classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is your turn to identify the word on the screen for the sound association game.

STUDENT: Come on, we just had finals, we're tired. I need some help with this one.

TUTOR: I will give you a hint. The word starts with a 'ch' sound.

STUDENT: Oh, then the word is 'champion'.

TUTOR: That is correct, but no point earned because I had to help you.

STUDENT: No point?!

options.A: Implementing genuine multicultural curricula that address race and disability, acknowledging student 'realities', and treating students as respected sources of knowledge during classroom activities.
options.B: Asking metacognitive questions about the purpose and value of the game (e.g., 'Why is this word identification important?' 'How will this help us read?').
options.C: Implementing relatively tight timelines for the student to identify the words during their turn in the sound association game over the coming weeks.
options.D: Offering support during the sound association game over several weeks until the student is able to participate and identify the words completely independently.
